# `silk/hash_set`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Hash sets that own their elements, with deterministic seeded hashing.

## When to use
Use [`HashSet`](#HashSet) to test membership fast, or to keep one copy of each value. The element type
must implement `silk.hash.HashKey`. Use `silk.list.List` when order or duplicate values matter.

## Details
[`HashSet.make`](#HashSet.impl.make) does not allocate. The first insert allocates eight buckets. The set doubles
the number of buckets before more than three quarters of them are in use. A failed growth leaves
the elements, the length, and the bucket count unchanged.

The same seed and the same operations give the same bucket order on each target. To visit each
element, scan the buckets from 0 to [`HashSet.bucketCount`](#HashSet.impl.bucketCount), test [`HashSet.occupiedAt`](#HashSet.impl.occupiedAt), and
read [`HashSet.elementAt`](#HashSet.impl.elementAt). This order is the bucket order, not the order of insertion.

## Gotchas
Each lookup consumes its probe value. If an equal element is already in the set, an insert keeps
the old element and drops the new one. [`HashSet.elementAt`](#HashSet.impl.elementAt) copies, so the element type must be
`Copy`. [`HashSet.contains`](#HashSet.impl.contains) and [`HashSet.indexOf`](#HashSet.impl.indexOf) work for elements that are not `Copy`.

## Examples
### Count the different values in a list
```silk
import silk.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.effect { Effect }
import silk.hash { Hash, Word }
import silk.hash_set { HashSet }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut seen = HashSet<Word>.make(Hash.seed(17))
  let values: [u64; 5] = [3, 1, 3, 2, 1]
  let mut index: usize = 0
  while index < 5 {
    let duplicate = run HashSet<Word>.insert(&mut seen, Hash.word(values[index]))
      |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
    index = index + 1
  }
  if HashSet<Word>.length(&seen) != 3 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="HashSet"></a>

## `HashSet`

```silk
pub struct HashSet<T>
```

A hash set that owns unique elements, with deterministic seeded hashing.

### When to use

Use it to test membership fast, or to keep one copy of each value. The element type must
implement `silk.hash.HashKey`. Use `silk.list.List` when order or duplicate values matter.

### Details

[`HashSet.make`](#HashSet.impl.make) does not allocate. The first insert allocates eight buckets. The set doubles
the number of buckets before more than three quarters of them are in use. A failed growth leaves
the elements, the length, and the bucket count unchanged.

To visit each element, scan the buckets from 0 to [`HashSet.bucketCount`](#HashSet.impl.bucketCount), test
[`HashSet.occupiedAt`](#HashSet.impl.occupiedAt), and read [`HashSet.elementAt`](#HashSet.impl.elementAt). This order is the bucket order, not the
order of insertion. The same seed and the same operations give the same bucket order on each
target.

Each element is unique under `HashKey.equals`. An insert of an element that is already present
keeps the old element. The set uses one seed for all of its hashes. Dropping the set drops each
element and then releases the storage.

### Gotchas

Each lookup consumes its probe value. [`HashSet.elementAt`](#HashSet.impl.elementAt) copies, so the element type must be
`Copy`. [`HashSet.contains`](#HashSet.impl.contains) and [`HashSet.indexOf`](#HashSet.impl.indexOf) work for elements that are not `Copy`.

#### Details

The seed and the sequence of operations decide the bucket order.

<a id="HashSet.impl.occupiedAt"></a>

### Method `occupiedAt`


Returns `true` if the bucket at `index` holds an element. Returns `false` for an index out of
range.

<a id="HashSet.impl.insert"></a>

### Method `insert`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn insert<T: HashKey + 'env, 'env>(
    self: &mut Self,
    value: T
  ) -> bool ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds `value` to the set. Returns `true` if the set already held an equal element, or `false`
if `value` is new.

#### Details

If an equal element is already present, the set does not change and drops `value`. The set
keeps the element that it already held.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the table must grow and the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. The
  set does not change.

<a id="HashSet.impl.contains"></a>

### Method `contains`

```silk
pub fn contains<T: HashKey>(self: &Self, value: T) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the set holds an element equal to `value`.

#### Details

This function consumes `value`. It does not change the set.

<a id="HashSet.impl.indexOf"></a>

### Method `indexOf`

```silk
pub fn indexOf<T: HashKey>(self: &Self, value: T) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the bucket index of the element equal to `value`, or `None` if there is no such
element.

#### When to use

Use `indexOf` to find an element without a copy or a move, for example when the element type
is not `Copy`.

#### Details

This function consumes `value`. It does not change the set.

<a id="HashSet.impl.remove"></a>

### Method `remove`

```silk
pub fn remove<T: HashKey>(self: &mut Self, value: T) -> Option<T>
```

Removes the element equal to `value` and returns the stored element. Returns `None` if there
is no such element.

#### Details

The caller owns the returned element. This function consumes `value`. It does not allocate.

<a id="HashSet.impl.elementAt"></a>

### Method `elementAt`

```silk
pub fn elementAt<T: Copy>(self: &Self, index: usize) -> T
```

Returns a copy of the element in the bucket at `index`.

#### When to use

Use `elementAt` with [`HashSet.occupiedAt`](#HashSet.impl.occupiedAt) to visit each element in bucket order.

#### Gotchas

The element type must be `Copy`. If `index` is out of range or the bucket is empty, the
program traps.
